nina_newhire: Hi all — onboarding benefits/payroll Qs from week 1. 1) I saw both HSA and FSA as options 5 which should I pick if I plan to enroll in the company's HSA-eligible HDHP? 2) How does the 401(k) match vesting work if I leave within the first 2 years? 3) I had to pay a $275 visa fee to relocate  is that reimbursable or expensed differently? 4) Do floating holidays carry over if unused?

sophie (People Ops): Welcome Nina! :wave: Quick bullets: HSA eligibility requires enrolling in the HSA-eligible HDHP. If you choose that plan, you can enroll in the HSA instead of a general-purpose FSA; general-purpose FSA will make you ineligible for HSA. Limited-purpose FSA (dental/vision only) is an option if you want FSA flexibility with HSA. 401(k) match/vesting and relocation/visa reimbursements below.

ben (Benefits): HSA vs FSA short:
- HSA: available only with HDHP. Pre-tax contributions, employer contribution (if any) + you keep the balance year-to-year. Great if you expect low near-term medical spend and want tax-advantaged savings.
- FSA: use-it-or-lose-it (plan year), good for predictable near-term medical expenses. If you elect a general-purpose FSA, you cannot contribute to HSA. If you want both, consider HDHP + limited-purpose FSA (dental/vision).

ben (Benefits): Enrollment logistics: pick plans in Rippling within 14 days of start. Effective dates still follow the standard first-of-month-after-30-days rule unless you elected expedited enrollment during offer.

nina_newhire: thanks  i enrolled HDHP + HSA in Rippling. Does the company contribute to HSA?

sophie (People Ops): We have a company HSA contribution for full-time employees. Amounts vary by tier; benefits docs show the current contribution schedule in the benefits packet. Ben can confirm the exact amount for 2026.

ben (Benefits): For 2026: company contributes $600/year for single and $1,200/year for family (pro-rated by hire date). Employer contributions post after your coverage effective date and show in the HSA account within 1-2 pay cycles.

nina_newhire: got it. 401(k) vesting? i'm thinking about early departures and want to understand what happens to the match if i leave within the first year.

mike_payroll: 401(k) basics: automatic enrollment at 3% deferral unless you opt-out or change it in Rippling > Payroll > 401(k). Employer match is subject to a vesting schedule; see below.

alec_finance: Vesting: Redwood's employer match vests pro-rata over 4 years (25% per year) with no cliff. So if you leave after 18 months, you'd be 37.5% vested (18/48 months * 100). Employer contributions that are not vested are forfeited per plan rules. The plan doc is the source of record; benefits packet has the summary and a link to the provider (Betterment portal).

nina_newhire: helpful. thanks. about the visa fee: i had to pay $275 to get paperwork processed before my start. Any way to expense that?

sophie (People Ops): Visa/immigration fees depend on the type. For relocation-related costs we may reimburse certain administrative expenses; please submit a note to relocations@redwood.com and cc benefits/finance with the receipt. Ben/Finance will confirm eligibility. If it's eligible, finance processes as a reimbursement via payroll.

alec_finance: If approved, submit via Ramp (category: Relocation & Onboarding) or use the expense form and cc finance@redwood.com. Example note: 

```
Expense: Employment visa processing fee
Amount: $275.00
Date: 2026-07-05
Receipt: attached
Category: Relocation & Onboarding
Notes: One-time relocation/immigration admin fee
```

alec_finance: Approved reimbursements are paid in the next payroll run unless marked urgent. We try to process relocations within 5 business days after approval.

hr-bot: Reminder: New hire benefits enrollment due by 2026-07-19. Complete elections in Rippling to avoid default plan selection.

nina_newhire: floating holidays? do those roll over?

sophie (People Ops): Floating holidays do not carry over year-to-year by default; we encourage using them within the calendar year. In exceptional business cases we can authorize carryover with manager + People Ops approval (we document it in Rippling).

nina_newhire: thank you! last thing: if i want to change my 401(k) deferral, how do i do that quickly?

mike_payroll: Update Rippling > Payroll > Retirement elections. Example to set to 6%: in Rippling change "Employee deferral" to "6%". If you want us to confirm it's taken before the next payroll cutoff, tag payroll and we'll verify.

nina_newhire: perfect, doing that now. Appreciate the quick answers everyone :pray:
